{{Short description|Icelandic mathematician (1903–1990)}}
'''Leifur Ásgeirsson''' (25 May 1903 – 19 August 1990) was the first Icelandic mathematician to gain major international recognition.<ref name=MacT>{{cite web|website=MacTutor|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Societies/Icelandic/|title=The Icelandic Mathematical Society}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Leifur Ásgeirsson graduated in 1927 from [[Reykjavik Junior College]] and received his doctorate in 1933 from the [[University of Göttingen]]. His doctoral advisor was [[Richard Courant]]. From 1931 to 1943 Leifur Ásgeirsson was the head of a district school in [[Þingeyjarsveit|Laugar]], located in southwestern Iceland's Reykjadalur Valley east of [[Reykjavík]].<ref name=MacT/> In 1936 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Oslo.<ref>{{cite book|author=Ásgeirsson, Leifur|pages=51–52|volume=Tome II|title=Comptes rendus du Congrès international des mathématiciens, Oslo 1936|chapter=Ein Mittelwertsatz für die Lösungen von <math display="inline">\sum_{i=1}^n \Big(\frac {\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2_i} - \frac {\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2_i} \Big) = 0 </math> angewandt auf zwei Potentialfunktionen |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1936.2/ICM1936.2.ocr.pdf}}</ref> At the [[University of Iceland]] he was appointed in 1943 a lecturer in mathematics and in 1945 a full professor of mathematics.<ref name=MacT/>

The journal ''{{ill|Mathematica Scandinavica|fr}}'' was founded in 1953 with Ásgeirsson as one of the founding editors.<ref name="Branner2003">{{cite journal|last1=Branner|first1=Bodil|authorlink=Bodil Branner|title=On the foundation of Mathematica Scandinavica|journal=Mathematica Scandinavica|volume=93|issue=1|year=2003|pages=5–18|issn=1903-1807|doi=10.7146/math.scand.a-14409|doi-access=free}} (See p. 12.)</ref>

{{blockquote|... ''Mathematica Scandinavica'' ... editors were appointed. From Denmark: [[Werner Fenchel|Fenchel]], from Finland: [[Gustav Elfving]], from Iceland: Leifur Ásgeirsson, from Norway: [[Thoralf Skolem|Skolem]], and from Sweden: [[Åke Pleijel|Pleijel]]. Immediately after the decisions had been taken Fenchel, in agreement with Pleijel, wrote to the other editors and suggested Bundgaard as co-ordinating editor of ''Math. Scand.''<ref name="Branner2003"/>}}
